answer: Sybil resistance is a first-light fresco gate. Each applicant books one east-facing lime panel and receives a uniquely milled cake of mineral pigment. Only in the official dawn window may they trowel that cake onto the damp panel; a loft-banded sparrow must then cross the wet field so its wing cutoff bakes into the crust under that morning's light. Graders match cake serial, panel stamp, and the observatory's dawn plate. Shared panels, leftover cakes, or later-hour photos are slashed as one farm. Fielding N keys costs N panels, N cakes, and N live dawn crossings that cannot share a morning.
